subject: religious-studies
topicDisplay: Christianity: Beliefs, Marriage & the Family, Living the Christian Life, Matters of Life & Death (Spec A)
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: According to the doctrine of the Trinity, God exists as which three persons?
options: The Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit
The Father, Mary and the Son
God, the angels and the saints
The Creator, the Prophet and the Church
questions.explain: The Trinity is the belief that there is one God in three persons: the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit.

questions.q: Which Christian statement of belief sets out the Church's teaching about the Trinity?
options: The Nicene Creed
The Ten Commandments
The Beatitudes
The Lord's Prayer
questions.explain: The Nicene Creed summarises core Christian beliefs, including belief in the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit.

questions.q: What does the Christian belief in the Incarnation mean?
options: That God became human in the person of Jesus
That Jesus rose from the dead
That God created the universe from nothing
That believers are reborn through baptism
questions.explain: The Incarnation is the belief that God took human form, becoming fully God and fully human in Jesus.

questions.q: In Christian belief, what is meant by atonement?
options: Jesus' death reconciles humanity with God and repairs the damage caused by sin
God's power to create the world out of nothing
The three persons of one God
The command to love your neighbour as yourself
questions.explain: Atonement is the belief that Christ's sacrifice restores the broken relationship between God and humanity.

questions.q: A Christian says: 'I cannot earn my way to heaven; salvation is a free, undeserved gift from God.' Which idea best expresses this belief?
options: Salvation through grace
Salvation through good works alone
Original sin
The sanctity of life
questions.explain: Grace is God's freely given, unearned love that offers salvation as a gift rather than a reward.

questions.q: In John's Gospel, through whom does God create everything at the beginning?
options: The Word (Logos), identified with Jesus
The archangel Gabriel
Adam
The prophets
questions.explain: John 1 teaches that all things were made through the Word, who is Jesus, showing his role in creation.

questions.q: What is the traditional Roman Catholic teaching on divorce?
options: Marriage is a lifelong bond that cannot be dissolved by divorce
Divorce is encouraged whenever a couple is unhappy
Divorce is allowed but remarriage is forbidden for everyone
There are no teachings about marriage in Catholicism
questions.explain: The Catholic Church teaches that marriage is indissoluble, reflecting 'what God has joined together, let no one separate.'

questions.q: Which of the following best describes the purposes of marriage in Christian teaching?
options: Companionship, the raising of children, and faithful sexual union
Financial gain and social status only
A temporary arrangement that can end at any time
A ceremony required to inherit property
questions.explain: Christians commonly see marriage as being for lifelong companionship, procreation and a faithful sexual relationship.

questions.q: What is the Roman Catholic Church's teaching on artificial contraception?
options: It opposes artificial contraception but permits natural family planning
It requires all couples to use artificial contraception
It has no teaching on contraception at all
It permits all forms of contraception without limit
questions.explain: The Catholic Church rejects artificial contraception but allows natural methods of regulating conception.

questions.q: What is meant by cohabitation?
options: A couple living together in a sexual relationship without being married
A couple who have divorced but still see each other
A religious ceremony blessing a marriage
A vow of lifelong celibacy
questions.explain: Cohabitation is living together as a couple without being married, which many traditional Christians discourage.

questions.q: A Christian argues that the family exists mainly to bring up children within the faith and to care for one another. Which role of the family does this describe?
options: Procreation and the education of children in a faith
Rejecting the wider community
Ending the practice of worship at home
Opposing all forms of marriage
questions.explain: Many Christians see a key purpose of the family as having children and bringing them up in the Christian faith.

questions.q: Which of the following best defines liturgical worship?
options: Worship that follows a set structure or order, often including the Eucharist
Worship with no set pattern and spontaneous prayer
Private prayer said alone at home
Silent meditation with no words at all
questions.explain: Liturgical worship follows a set, formal order of service, such as the Catholic Mass or Anglican Eucharist.

questions.q: Which of these is a well-known Christian pilgrimage site associated with healing?
options: Lourdes
Mecca
The River Ganges
Bodh Gaya
questions.explain: Lourdes in France is a major Christian pilgrimage site linked with prayer for healing and the Virgin Mary.

questions.q: What is the main difference between believers' baptism and infant baptism?
options: Believers' baptism is for those old enough to declare their own faith, while infant baptism is for babies
Believers' baptism uses no water, while infant baptism uses water
Infant baptism can only take place at Easter
There is no difference between them
questions.explain: Believers' baptism requires a personal declaration of faith, whereas infant baptism welcomes a baby into the Church.

questions.q: A church runs a food bank and supports a charity working overseas to relieve poverty. Which aspect of Christian life is this an example of?
options: Serving the local and worldwide community through charity
Liturgical worship
Pilgrimage
Celebrating the sacraments
questions.explain: Practical care such as food banks and charity work reflects the Christian call to serve both local and global communities.

questions.q: Which Christian belief does the festival of Christmas mainly celebrate?
options: The Incarnation and birth of Jesus
The resurrection of Jesus
The giving of the Holy Spirit at Pentecost
The ascension of Jesus into heaven
questions.explain: Christmas celebrates the birth of Jesus, marking the Christian belief in the Incarnation of God as a human.

questions.q: What does the Christian principle of the sanctity of life mean?
options: Life is holy and sacred because it is created and given by God
Only human life over the age of 18 has value
Life has value only if a person is healthy
Life belongs to the state rather than to God
questions.explain: The sanctity of life is the belief that all life is sacred because it is God-given, made in the image of God.

questions.q: How do many Christians respond to the scientific Big Bang theory of the origin of the universe?
options: They accept it as the method God used to create the universe
They all reject any scientific explanation completely
They believe the universe has always existed unchanged
They teach that the universe was not created at all
questions.explain: Many Christians see no conflict, viewing the Big Bang as the process through which God brought creation into being.

questions.q: In debates about abortion, what is the difference between 'sanctity of life' and 'quality of life' arguments?
options: Sanctity of life stresses that all life is sacred, while quality of life considers the wellbeing a person can expect
Sanctity of life applies only to adults, quality of life only to children
They both mean exactly the same thing
Quality of life means life is God-given and cannot be ended
questions.explain: Sanctity of life arguments defend life as God-given and sacred, whereas quality of life weighs a person's expected wellbeing.

questions.q: A Christian opposes euthanasia, saying: 'Only God has the right to give and take life.' Which belief is this based on?
options: The sanctity of life
The quality of life
The theory of evolution
The purpose of pilgrimage
questions.explain: The belief that life is sacred and belongs to God leads many Christians to reject euthanasia.

specSource: Pearson Edexcel GCSE Religious Studies A (1RA0) specification; Christianity: Beliefs, Marriage & the Family, Living the Christian Life, Matters of Life & Death (Spec A)
